requirements:
# Mechanical Arm Control - **Difficulty:** Hard (hard) ## Requirements Design a PLC program to control an automated mechanical arm that performs handling tasks on the production line. The mechanical arm has six basic actions: down, up, left, right, grip, and release. The operating modes of the mechanical arm include four types: manual, single step, single cycle, and continuous. Control requirements: 1. Manual mode: Allows the operator to control each action of the mechanical arm individually through the control panel, provided it is not yet in position. For example, pressing the down button (DownButton=1), if not at the down position (DownLimitSwitch=0), then move down (MoveDown=1); if at the down position (DownLimitSwitch=1), stop moving down. Releasing the down button also stops the movement down. 2. Single step mode: The mechanical arm automatically executes one action according to the preset program, and the operator needs to confirm after each action is completed to execute the next action. The initial position of the mechanical arm is at the top left. When the start button is pressed once, the mechanical arm executes the down command MoveDown, and stops after reaching the down position. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the grip command ActivateGrip, and stops after gripping. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the up command MoveUp, and stops after reaching the up position. When the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm executes the right command MoveRight, and stops after reaching the right position. When the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm executes the down command MoveDown, and stops after reaching the down position. When the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm executes the release command ActivateRelease, and stops after releasing. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the up command MoveUp, and stops after reaching the up position. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the left command MoveLeft, and stops after reaching the left position. Then starts the cycle again from the beginning 3. Single cycle mode: The mechanical arm automatically completes a full handling cycle, including all preset actions, and stops at the end of the cycle waiting for the operator's instruction. The initial position of the mechanical arm is at the top left, when the start button is pressed: The mechanical arm first moves down, then grips after reaching the down position, moves up after gripping, moves right after reaching the up position, moves down after reaching the right position, releases after reaching the down position, moves up after releasing, moves left after reaching the up position, and stops after reaching the left position. 4. Continuous mode: The initial position of the mechanical arm is at the top left, when the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm continuously executes the handling cycle of the single cycle mode. 5. The emergency stop function can stop all actions of the mechanical arm at any time. Use GripLimitSwitch and ReleaseLimitSwitch as the completion feedback for gripping and releasing respectively. The caller keeps the four mode-selection inputs mutually exclusive. ## Interface Definition | Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Input | `ManualMode` | `BOOL` | Manual mode | | Input | `SingleStepMode` | `BOOL` | Single step mode | | Input | `SingleCycleMode` | `BOOL` | Single cycle mode | | Input | `ContinuousMode` | `BOOL` | Continuous mode | | Input | `EmergencyStop` | `BOOL` | Emergency stop signal
FALSE: Emergency stop triggered
TRUE: No emergency stop triggered | | Input | `Start` | `BOOL` | Start operation | | Input | `DownButton` | `BOOL` | Down button | | Input | `UpButton` | `BOOL` | Up button | | Input | `LeftButton` | `BOOL` | Left button | | Input | `RightButton` | `BOOL` | Right button | | Input | `GripButton` | `BOOL` | Grip button | | Input | `ReleaseButton` | `BOOL` | Release button | | Input | `DownLimitSwitch` | `BOOL` | Down position limit switch | | Input | `UpLimitSwitch` | `BOOL` | Up position limit switch | | Input | `LeftLimitSwitch` | `BOOL` | Left position limit switch | | Input | `RightLimitSwitch` | `BOOL` | Right position limit switch | | Input | `GripLimitSwitch` | `BOOL` | Grip position limit switch | | Input | `ReleaseLimitSwitch` | `BOOL` | Release position limit switch | | Output | `MoveDown` | `BOOL` | Down command | | Output | `MoveUp` | `BOOL` | Up command | | Output | `MoveLeft` | `BOOL` | Left command | | Output | `MoveRight` | `BOOL` | Right command | | Output | `ActivateGrip` | `BOOL` | Grip command | | Output | `ActivateRelease` | `BOOL` | Release command |

interface.name: EmergencyStop
interface.description:
Emergency stop signal
FALSE: Emergency stop triggered
TRUE: No emergency stop triggered

scan_semantics: Inputs I[k] are sampled at invocation; outputs O[k] are observed after the call. Retained pre-state q[k] becomes q[k+1]. Each test resets the instance. A transition affects the same observed scan. dt_ms is elapsed time since the preceding invocation; the first invocation starts IEC timers at elapsed zero. CycleTime inputs, where supplied, are attributed to the current invocation rather than inferred from dt_ms.
safety_priority: Emergency stop overrides every mode and request.
Opposed directions and grip/release are mutually exclusive.
A reached position suppresses its own command immediately.
assumptions: EmergencyStop=FALSE cancels the sequence and outputs; recovery requires a fresh Start edge from a verified top-left pose.
A Start press is a rising edge. Start edges during an active action are ignored; edge history still updates.
No selected mode means all commands off and sequence reset. Changing mode also resets the sequence.
Opposing manual commands on an axis or grip pair are both inhibited. Independent non-opposing actions may run together.
Manual commands are combinational and stop on their matching limit/feedback. Contradictory limit switches are outside the caller contract.

Only one phase transition occurs per invocation. In cycle modes, completion feedback switches to the next command in that scan; an already-active next limit suppresses its command but is processed as completion on the next invocation.
Single-step completion switches all outputs off; the next action requires a fresh Start edge on a later scan.
Continuous completion of left movement wraps to down in the same scan. Single-cycle completion returns to idle.

At the start of a new automatic sequence (action 1, not every individual single step), UpLimitSwitch and LeftLimitSwitch must both be TRUE. Grip and release complete on the supplied feedback switches.

atomic_propositions.no_mode: none of the four mode selectors TRUE
atomic_propositions.exclusive: NOT(MoveDown AND MoveUp) AND NOT(MoveLeft AND MoveRight) AND NOT(ActivateGrip AND ActivateRelease)
atomic_propositions.down_manual: ManualMode AND DownButton AND NOT UpButton AND NOT DownLimitSwitch
atomic_propositions.step_done: SingleStepMode AND pre-busy AND matching completion feedback
atomic_propositions.waiting: SingleStepMode AND NOT pre-busy AND NOT rising(Start)
atomic_propositions.cycle_done: SingleCycleMode AND pre-phase LEFT AND LeftLimitSwitch
atomic_propositions.continuous_done: ContinuousMode AND pre-phase LEFT AND LeftLimitSwitch
atomic_propositions.begin_next: post-phase DOWN with command gated by DownLimitSwitch
atomic_propositions.feedback: matching completion feedback for the pre-action is TRUE
atomic_propositions.start: fresh Start edge in idle with top-left pose and selected automatic mode
atomic_propositions.ordered: the next accepted automatic phase follows DOWN, GRIP, UP1, RIGHT, DOWN2, RELEASE, UP2, LEFT

ltl.name: Safety
ltl.explanation: No command survives emergency stop or no mode.

ltl.name: Interlocks
ltl.explanation: Opposed actuators are never commanded together.

ltl.name: Manual down
ltl.explanation: Manual down requires the button and an unreached lower limit.

ltl.name: Reached limits
ltl.explanation: Every corresponding completion input suppresses its command.

ltl.name: Step wait
ltl.explanation: A completed single step waits for another press.

ltl.name: Automatic start
ltl.explanation: A permitted fresh start begins down.

ltl.name: Order
ltl.explanation: The eight preset actions retain their required order.

ltl.name: Conditional liveness
ltl.formula: (G(safe & SingleCycleMode) & G(busy -> F feedback)) -> G(started -> F idle)
ltl.explanation: With unchanged safe single-cycle mode and eventual matching feedback, every started sequence eventually returns idle.

tests.name: manual_limits
tests.purpose: Manual hold-to-run, reached limits, opposing requests and emergency priority.

tests.name: single_step
tests.purpose: Each new step requires a release and fresh start; held start cannot skip grip.

tests.name: single_cycle
tests.purpose: All eight actions complete once and wait at top left.

tests.name: continuous
tests.purpose: The eighth completion wraps immediately to the first action.

tests.name: emergency_reset
tests.purpose: Emergency cancels an action; releasing emergency does not auto-restart.
